source.title: Picky LLMs and Unreliable RMs: An Empirical Study on Safety Alignment after Instruction Tuning
source.authors: Guan-Lin Li; Kangjie Chen; Shangwei Guo; Jie Zhang; Han Qiu; Chao Zhang; Guo-Yin Wang; Tian-Wei Zhang; Ji-Wei Li

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether benign instruction tuning changes harmful-request safety, using LoRA tuning and SALAD-Bench jailbreak success rates; it does not reproduce the original study’s method and measure exactly.
record.gate_note: Table 1 reports general (SAg) and adversarial (SAa) jailbreak success rates for the untuned models and seven benign tuning conditions. Lower SA means higher safety. Rows below record each tuned model, dataset, and metric separately. The paper also reports identity-calibration and role-play conditions in Table 2 and subset-selection results in Figure 2; those additional results are not included in the rows.
record.test_reason: The study LoRA-tunes three safety-aligned instruct models (Llama-3-8B, Mistral-7B, Qwen2-7B) on purely benign datasets. It measures SALAD-Bench jailbreak success on general and attack-enhanced harmful questions, so its results bear directly on V2. It is T5 rather than plain T2 because it argues V2 needs restating: erosion depends on answer format, identity calibration and role-play, and some benign datasets maintain or improve safety. It does not test V1 or V3–V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly wrong. The authors say benign fine-tuning degrades safety in most cases on the original datasets. They show that answer format, identity calibration and role-play can be adjusted to raise or lower safety: Markdown formatting and identity calibration keep or improve it, role-play usually harms it. They also find reward models unreliable for selecting data that preserves safety. The record's 'increase or maintain' phrasing echoes one sentence but omits the degradation finding.
record.recipe_differences: Uses benign downstream instruction datasets and LoRA fine-tuning, then evaluates harmful-request jailbreak success with SALAD-Bench; it does not use the original harmful-data setup or its safety measure.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary by model, dataset, answer reformatting, and whether evaluation uses general or adversarial harmful questions. The paper also states that evaluation disables sampling and uses no system prompt.

fits_no_version.finding: Training and validation loss track the safety change. Reformatting lowers loss on Med, Pyt and OP and raises it on CRAFTSG, mirroring SA (Table 10). Role-play changes safety without changing loss (Table 11).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign-tuning safety erosion scales with distribution mismatch (loss) between tuning data and the model's post-training answer style.

fits_no_version.finding: Open-source reward models disagree on top and bottom data subsets and mostly score reformatted (safer) data lower than the originals (Table 3, Figure 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reward-model scores fail to predict the safety effect of benign tuning data.

record.problems: Open-source models only; English datasets only; LoRA fine-tuning only. The reported safety measure depends on the SALAD-Bench judge. No uncertainty estimates are reported in Table 1.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 reports additional identity-calibration and role-play tuning conditions, and Figure 2 reports safety after selecting MedicalInstruct subsets by five reward models. These are not transcribed into rows; the rows here cover Table 1’s main dataset and answer-reformatting comparisons.

untested.parts: Full-parameter fine-tuning (LoRA only); varying data volume or few-shot benign sets; closed or commercial models; any effect of system prompts (none used); non-English data; harmfulness scores other than the SALAD-Bench judge.
No prefilling or decoding attacks; SAa uses attack-enhanced prompts only as an evaluation set.
No test of why alignment is shallow.

missing.what: Failure-case comparison for reformatted datasets on Llama-3 (e.g. OP reformat before checking SAa 29.46 vs 32.16 after); changes stated as usually under 1%.

record.verdict_notes: Table 2, declared in rows_left_out, holds the strongest benign erosion. Reformatted CRAFTSG with identity statements removed raises Llama-3 to 39.32/90.44, and to 64.22/96.44 with role-play added. Researchers should consult it, since it shows CRAFTSG's apparent safety comes from its embedded AI-identity and refusal text. The text contains a self-contradiction: it says fine-tuning 'will decrease both SAg and SAa' in most cases, yet elsewhere claims benign datasets 'increase or maintain' safety. No uncertainty estimates are given; evaluation is greedy decoding with no system prompt, 5,000 questions per metric.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful fine-tuning examples are used.
Tests only the paper’s benign datasets and specified dataset transformations; it does not test arbitrary benign instruction data or few-shot data volumes.
No per-token KL divergence or response-position measurement.
No compliant-opening prefills, suffix attacks, or decoding-change intervention.
No localization of safety to weights or ranks.
The paper proposes explanations for sensitivity to dataset features, but does not test why safety alignment is shallow in the first-token sense.
No intervention intended to deepen safety across response tokens.

relationships.condition: Original-format MedicalInstruct, PythonCodeInstruct and OpenPlatypus (and CRAFTSG on Mistral SAg)
relationships.reason: Benign tuning raises jailbreak success, e.g. Llama-3 SAa 36.70→95.82 (Med) and 73.38 (Pyt), Mistral SAg 16.00→46.70 (OP).
relationships.display_finding: Jailbreak success rose, for example Llama-3 SAa from 36.70 to 95.82 with MedicalInstruct and to 73.38 with PythonCodeInstruct, and Mistral SAg from 16.00 to 46.70 with OpenPlatypus.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Original-format MedicalInstruct, PythonCodeInstruct and OpenPlatypus (and CRAFTSG on Mistral SAg)
source_check.reason: The specified supporting rows increase jailbreak success; Table 1 confirms the cited values and baselines.

relationships.condition: Same datasets with answers reformatted into itemized Markdown by an aligned LLM
relationships.reason: Reformatting removes or reverses erosion in most cases, e.g. L3-PytR-SAa 36.68 vs 73.38 original and Q2-OPR-SAa 64.76. Some cases stay elevated (L3-MedR-SAa 70.28, M-MedR-SAg 37.68).
relationships.display_finding: Erosion was removed or reversed in most cases, e.g. Llama-3 on Python data scored 36.68 versus 73.38 with the original answers, though some medical cases stayed elevated (70.28 and 37.68).

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Same datasets with answers reformatted into itemized Markdown by an aligned LLM
source_check.reason: Table 1 shows mixed outcomes after reformatting, including persistent erosion, near-baseline rates, and improved safety. Section 4.1 identifies Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct as the reformatter.

relationships.condition: Original datasets where the effect depends on model or metric (Qwen2 generally; SAg on Pyt/OP for Llama-3 and Qwen2)
relationships.reason: Erosion is small or absent on one metric, e.g. Q2-Med-SAa 86.50→88.12 and L3-Pyt-SAg 4.44→4.32, while the other metric rises.
relationships.display_finding: Erosion was small or absent on one metric while the other rose, e.g. Qwen2 medical SAa went from 86.50 to 88.12 and Llama-3 Python SAg from 4.44 to 4.32.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Original datasets where the effect depends on model or metric (Qwen2 generally; SAg on Pyt/OP for Llama-3 and Qwen2)
source_check.reason: Table 1 confirms small increases or decreases on the listed model–metric combinations, supporting model- and metric-dependent qualification.

relationships.condition: CRAFTSG (GPT-4-generated Singapore culture data) on Llama-3 and Qwen2, and Mistral SAa
relationships.reason: No rise or a drop in jailbreak success: L3 SAa 36.70→28.98, Q2 SAa 86.50→79.32, Mistral SAa 93.80→92.82. This is qualified by the data's built-in identity and refusal text.
relationships.display_finding: SAa jailbreak success fell for Llama-3 (36.70 to 28.98), Qwen2 (86.50 to 79.32) and Mistral (93.80 to 92.82), though the data includes built-in identity and refusal text.

relation.reason: The study measures harmful-response success before and after benign LoRA instruction-tuning, directly testing V2.

tranche.reason: Sections 4.1–4.2 and Table 1 directly qualify benign-tuning erosion: safety can improve or deteriorate depending on answer format, identity calibration, role-play, model, and evaluation setting.

source_check.notes: SA values are percentages; each metric uses 5,000 SALAD-Bench questions. Evaluation uses no system prompt and disables sampling; no uncertainty analysis establishes equivalence for the tiny baseline differences.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: MedicalInstruct, PythonCodeInstruct, and OpenPlatypus conditions with increased SA values
reader_labels.reason: Higher reported jailbreak success rates after benign tuning support erosion in these settings; see the linked rows.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: CRAFTSG and several reformatted or dataset-specific conditions across the tested models
reader_labels.reason: Some benign tuning conditions lower SA, indicating improved rather than eroded safety in those measurements.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Across models, datasets, answer formatting, and general versus adversarial harmful questions
reader_labels.reason: The effect is not uniform: the paper reports both increases and decreases, and the outcome varies by model, dataset, formatting, and metric.
